label: GO only, early episode: raised after reaching S2 (esp. unrewarded / rare a1), lowered after S1
terms: (phase == GO) * np.exp(-ep_trial/25) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp(-ep_trial/25) * (prev_state == S2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp(-ep_trial/25) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp(-ep_trial/25) * (prev_state == S2) * (prev_action == 1)
explanation: Fires only at GO, and mostly in the first ~50 trials of an episode (timing alone gives R^2 0.42). Beyond timing, the size depends on the previous trial reached state, scaled by an early-episode decay exp(-ep_trial/25). After S2 it is raised (weight +0.65), more after S2 unrewarded (+0.91 more) and after a1 -> S2 rare (+0.60 more). After S1 it is lowered (-1.12). Additive tables without the time interaction do much worse (0.28 dev): the previous-state effect shrinks along with the early-episode timing envelope. The trial before, the hidden good state, the value and the policy add little (<0.01). Some leftover variance: on early trials, large activations after S1 unrewarded are under-predicted. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.686 (total 0.82), above the profile all-cue additive ceiling of 0.39. Uses only observed cues.

issues: Reproduced test R^2 beyond timing 0.6858 (total 0.819, timing alone 0.42). The weights match the explanation: S2 +0.65, S2&unrewarded +0.91, S1 -1.12, S2&a1 +0.60.

The S2-vs-S1 contrast carries almost all of it: those two time-scaled terms alone reach test 0.604. Without the exp(-ep_trial/25) envelope the same four terms reach only 0.29, so the claim that the effect interacts with time holds up. The decay constant is not critical: tau=15 gives 0.636 and tau=40 gives 0.639.

Small mis-statement in the residual caveat. Misses show GO after S1 is under-predicted by about +0.03 for all four S1 patterns (a1 S1 u, a2 S1 r, a1 S1 r, a2 S1 u), rewarded or not. So the leftover error is not specific to 'S1 unrewarded'. The largest over-prediction is GO after a2 S2 r (-0.05).

The worst-fit windows are mostly the window's first trial, where the previous trial is unknown (prev_state=-1): about 2.5 actual vs 0.93 predicted. This is a window-edge artifact. Adding a prev_state==-1 term gains less than 0.001.

No large systematic gap remains. Each of these candidate additions gains 0.017 or less on dev: the trial before (state or reward two trials back), start_high, the hidden good state, the agent's upcoming choice (future), the first trials of the episode (ep_trial<5), and value/choice interactions. The best was value/choice x S2, +0.017.

Activations look close to binary (about 2-2.5 or 0), so some of the remaining variance may be all-or-none firing that a linear fit of magnitude cannot capture. It does not line up with any cue tested here.
